To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mandibular cartilage is an unusual secondary cartilage in which the expression pattern of the major non‐collageneous bone matrix protein bone sialoproteins is similar to that of primary cartilage.

bone sialoproteins are not expressed in the condylopathic cartilage until hypertrophic chonodrocytes are present, but the expression is more extensive and the hypertrophic chondrogenesis is more rapid than in the tibia.

the expression of bone sialo protein (BSP) mRNA is extensive in the hypertrophic cell zones of the condylar and tibial cartilages, and the expression of secreted phosphoprote in 1 (SPP1, osteopontein) mRNA is also extensive in the hypertropic cell zone of the condylal cartilage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of the mandibulart condylar cartilages in mouse fetuses and the expression of two non‐collagen matrix proteins.
the expression of two bone matrix proteins in the condylal cartilage and its comparison with that in limb bud cartilage.
the development of a new method for the detection of the formation process of a secondary cartilage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation process in the mandibular cartilage is more closely related to that in the primary cartilages than that in the secondary cartilages.
the condylar chondrocyte is a secondary chondrocytic cell that is not identical to the primary chondrocytical cell.
the condylar and tibial cartilages differ in their expression of BSP and that the condylus is a secondary cartilage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mandibular cartilage is a special type of cartilage that has some characteristics of both primary and secondary cartilage.
the condylar chondrocyte is more active than the tibial chondrocyt in terms of mineralization.
the condylar chondrocyte is an active chondrocytic cell, and that the condylus is a unique chondrogenic site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation process in the condylary cartilage is more rapid than that in the cartilage in the limb bud.
the mandibular cartilage is not a secondary cartilage.
